title: Koszul-regular ideal cancellation with split conormal sequence
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $K\subseteq J$ ideals, with $K$ finitely generated. Use localization at an element [def-weil-ring-localization-away] and finite Koszul-regular sequences [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Assume that for every prime $\mathfrak p\supseteq J$ there is $h\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ such that both $KR_h$ and $JR_h$ are generated by finite Koszul-regular sequences in $R_h$. Suppose the canonical sequence of $R/J$-modules
$$0\longrightarrow K/KJ\xrightarrow{\alpha}J/J^2\longrightarrow J/(K+J^2)\longrightarrow0$$
is exact and split, where $\alpha$ is induced by inclusion and split means that there is an $R/J$-linear map $r:J/J^2\to K/KJ$ with $r\alpha=\mathrm{id}$. Put $\overline R=R/K$ and $\overline J=J/K$. For every prime $\mathfrak q\supseteq\overline J$ of $\overline R$, there is $u\in\overline R\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that $\overline J\overline R_u$ is generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence in $\overline R_u$. Empty sequences are allowed; no Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 068Z (lemma-permanence-regular-immersion), assertion (3), affine ideal form; proof (3) and Tag 063G (lemma-regular-ideal-sheaf-scheme).

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak q\supseteq\overline J$ of $R/K$, and let $\mathfrak p$ be its inverse image in $R$. Thus $J\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Choose $h\notin\mathfrak p$ as in the hypothesis, and set $A=R_h$, $P=\mathfrak pA$, $I=KA$, $L=JA$. Both $I$ and $L$ have finite Koszul-regular generating sequences, so both fibre spaces below are finite dimensional. The prime $P$ consists of fractions with numerator in $\mathfrak p$; $A_P=R_{\mathfrak p}$ since both rings invert exactly the elements needed to invert every element outside $\mathfrak p$. Write $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)=A_P/PA_P$. These fraction descriptions identify $I_P=K_{\mathfrak p}$ and $L_P=J_{\mathfrak p}$.

source.place: Tag 068Z (lemma-permanence-regular-immersion), proof of assertion (3), affine ideal form.

proof.text: Tensor the given identity $r\alpha=1$ with $k$ over $R/J$. The resulting maps still compose to the identity: this is checked on $c\otimes x$ and hence on finite sums of pure tensors. There are explicit identifications $k\otimes_{R/J}(K/KJ)=K_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pK_{\mathfrak p}$ and $k\otimes_{R/J}(J/J^2)=J_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pJ_{\mathfrak p}$: send $c\otimes[a]$ to $c[a/1]$, with inverse $[a/t]\mapsto(1/t)\otimes[a]$. The balanced relations, $J\subseteq\mathfrak p$, and invertibility of $t\notin\mathfrak p$ verify these formulas and their inverse identities. Under them $1\otimes\alpha$ is the map $I_P/PI_P\to L_P/PL_P$ induced by inclusion. It therefore has a left inverse and is injective. Only the retraction identity is used; no exactness of tensoring with $k$ is required.

source.place: Tag 068Z (lemma-permanence-regular-immersion), proof of assertion (3), affine ideal form.

proof.text: Choose a basis of $I_P/PI_P$, and extend its injective image to a basis of $L_P/PL_P$, using [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-basis-through-vector]. The spaces are spanned by the images of finite generating lists of $I$ and $L$, so the bases are finite. Every basis vector in the first space is represented by $a/t$ with $a\in I$, $t\notin P$. Multiplying it by the nonzero scalar $t$ gives a representative $f_i\in I$ and preserves the basis. Extend the resulting image basis in the second space; likewise clear a denominator in each added basis vector to obtain representatives $g_j\in L$. Thus the images of $f_1,\ldots,f_n$ form a basis of $I_P/PI_P$, and those of $f_1,\ldots,f_n,g_1,\ldots,g_m$ form a basis of $L_P/PL_P$.

source.place: Tag 068Z (lemma-permanence-regular-immersion), proof of assertion (3), affine ideal form.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-koszul-generators-from-fibre-basis] first to $I\subseteq P$ with $(f_i)$ and then to $L\subseteq P$ with $(f_i,g_j)$. Obtain $s,t\in A\setminus P$ such that $(f_i)$ generates $IA_s$ and is Koszul-regular in $A_s$, while $(f_i,g_j)$ generates $LA_t$ and is Koszul-regular in $A_t$. Pass to $B=A_{st}$. The maps $A_s\to B$ and $A_t\to B$ are localizations, hence flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]; [lem-sc-koszul-regular-flat-base-change] makes both sequences Koszul-regular in $B$. The same generating identities hold in $B$, since localizing a finite linear combination localizes its coefficients.

source.place: Tag 068Z (lemma-permanence-regular-immersion), proof of assertion (3), affine ideal form.

proof.text: In $B$ we have $IB=(f_1,\ldots,f_n)$ and $LB=(f_1,\ldots,f_n,g_1,\ldots,g_m)$. The prefix and concatenation are both Koszul-regular. The forward implication of [lem-sfb-koszul-prefix-quotient-criterion] therefore makes $(\overline g_1,\ldots,\overline g_m)$ Koszul-regular in $C=B/IB$. Every element of $LB$ is a linear combination of the $f_i$ and $g_j$; modulo $IB$ precisely the $g_j$ remain, so they generate the image ideal $LB/IB$.

source.place: Tag 068M (lemma-truncate-koszul-regular), as used in divisors.tex Tag 068Z(3).

proof.text:
Write $s=a/h^e$ and $t=b/h^f$ with $a,b
otin\mathfrak p$, and put $v=hab
otin\mathfrak p$. Inverting $h$ and $st$ is the same as inverting $h,a,b$: an inverse to a product gives inverses to its factors by multiplying by the remaining factors. Thus $B=A_{st}$ is canonically $R_v$, by the fraction maps in [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-quotient-commute], $C=R_v/KR_v$ is canonically $(R/K)_u$, where $u=v mod K
otin\mathfrak q$; this map sends the image of $J$ to $\overline J(R/K)_u$. For the ring isomorphism $\phi$, the map $\sum_Tc_Te_T\mapsto\sum_T\phi(c_T)e_T$ on each exterior-basis Koszul term commutes with the differential, whose coefficients are the sequence entries [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex]. Its inverse uses $\phi^{-1}$, so it identifies kernels and images and preserves the homology vanishing. The transported $\overline g_j$ therefore give the required Koszul-regular generators on $(R/K)_u$. Since $\mathfrak q$ was arbitrary, this proves the assertion, also for empty tuples. If $R/K=0$ there is no such prime and the assertion is vacuous.
